Skill Card C

⚡ Typing Code

The same programs you build with blocks, typed in Python-style code. Start with words that match the blocks, then step up to the Python habits: quotes, = and ==.

Getting there: click any object, choose Program, and pick a level at the top of the panel: BlocksBasic BeginnerBasic Pro. Your blocks appear as code. Type, press Save, and it runs right away. Switch back any time — nothing is lost.

Two levels

Basic Beginner

Reads just like the blocks, word for word. Text needs no quotes.

forever move forward 10 feet rotate 90 degrees say Hello!

Basic Pro

The Python-style step up: text in quotes, no unit words, and = to set a number.

side = 10 forever move forward side rotate 90 say "Hello!"

Three rules

  1. One line, one action

    Every line is one block. It starts with a command word, like move, rotate, say or repeat.

  2. Push lines in to put them inside

    Lines pushed in by four spaces under repeat, forever, if or when are the ones it runs. Python works the same way. Press Enter after one of those lines and the editor pushes the next line in for you.

    repeat 4 times move forward 8 feet rotate 90 degrees say Done!

  3. A card tells you what to change

    If a line has a problem, it is underlined and a card under the code says what to do. When there is one clear answer, Fix it changes the line for you. Save waits until every line works, so nothing is ever lost.

Every command, at both levels

The same four colours as the blocks. Numbers are feet, seconds, degrees or percent, the same units the blocks use. Anywhere a number goes, a name works too: repeat sides times.

Type these four first

  1. Spin forever

    The two-line classic. Change the 15 and the speed changes.

    forever rotate 15 degrees

  2. Drive a square

    Four sides, four right turns. 360 ÷ 4 = 90, so it ends exactly where it started.

    repeat 4 times glide 8 feet over 2 seconds rotate 90 degrees

  3. A heartbeat, at Basic Pro

    set size to measures from the size the object started at, so this beats steadily forever instead of slowly growing.

    forever set size to 115 wait 0.4 set size to 100 wait 0.4

  4. Tell another object what to do

    Name an object from its menu (click it, then Name it), and tell talks to just that one.

    # on the first object: tell robot2 go
    # on the object named robot2: when an object says go glide 20 feet over 3 seconds

🤯 Worth knowing

Blocks, Basic Beginner and Basic Pro are three views of one program. Build with blocks, pick Basic Beginner, and your blocks appear as code you can read. Move up to Basic Pro and the same program is rewritten with quotes and =, the way Python writes it. The fastest way to learn is to build something with blocks first, then go and read what it says as code.

Where to practise
